findings.claim: Whether a `disputed` ledger blocks licensing and release is stated as settled behaviour in two places and simultaneously declared an unresolved owner call in three others, with one of those three explicitly warning that it must not be pre-empted. The two positions cannot both hold.
findings.evidence: ASSERTED AS SETTLED - rights-ownership-cx.md:91 (CX-03 detail): "`disputed` is a registry state that **freezes payouts and blocks every exploitation verdict** in a master's Control Summary." Same claim in the map row at rights-ownership-cx.md:21: "`disputed` freezes payouts and blocks every exploitation verdict." Implemented concretely at 09.01-rights-registry/09.01.03-master-rights-ownership.md:150 "| Release / distribute | An exclusive grant covering the target territory in the target window ([12](../../12-release-distribution/)); `unallocated` or `disputed` ledger |" and :151 "| Grant a non-exclusive master licence | The deterministic recorded master-action consent evaluator; `disputed` ledger |", and at :283 "| Disputed / frozen | Conflict raised via [09.04] | Dispute banner; payouts frozen; Control Summary blocks every exploitation action naming the dispute". These verdicts gate: 09.01.03:239 "Actions gated on that verdict stay gated." || DECLARED OPEN - 09.04-rights-conflicts-disputes/09.04.03-rights-freeze-royalty-escrow.md:112 "Q-04 | [OWNER] Does a freeze also block **licensing** and **release** of the contested work, or only payment? ... but the live-release and licensing halves are an unresolved values trade (blocking is the stronger lever and punishes uninvolved co-owners hardest)". Same at 09.04-rights-conflicts-disputes/09.04-rights-conflicts-disputes-index.md:61 "Q-02 | [OWNER] Does a dispute make the work **unusable** (release-blocked, licence-blocked) or only unpaid (escrowed)? ... A values trade, not a derivable fact". And 09.01-rights-registry/09.01.01-work-recording-duality.md:333 states the constraint explicitly: "Whether an *asserted* dispute then blocks release, or only escrows payment, is an open owner call - [09.04 Q-02] and [09.04.03 Q-04] - and **this row must not pre-empt it**."
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer building 09.01.03's Control Summary must decide, with no ratified answer, whether a `disputed` ledger returns `Blocked by` or `No recorded obstacle` for 'Release / distribute' and 'Grant a non-exclusive master licence'. The two candidate behaviours have opposite consequences for uninvolved co-owners of a partially-frozen ledger - the exact trade 09.04 Q-02 says only the owner can make.
findings.howToFix: Either narrow rights-ownership-cx.md CX-03 and 09.01.03's action table to the settled half only (payouts frozen; pre-delivery release ineligible per 12.01.01 D-07) and render the live-release and licensing rows as `Unknown - terms not recorded` pending 09.04.03 Q-04, mirroring the treatment 09.01.03 already gives its own Q-09 takedown row at :157; or ratify Q-04/09.04 Q-02 and delete the open markers.

findings.claim: The two files that own the publishing ledger give opposite answers to the most common path in the domain: whether the system creates a self-held publisher row for a writer who has not declared a publishing position. 09.01.02 says the row is auto-created and pre-filled and that a ledger with no publisher rows is valid; 09.01.04 says an undeclared position must never render as self-published and that only an explicit act creates the row.
findings.evidence: AUTO-CREATED - 09.01-rights-registry/09.01.02-ownership-ledger-validation.md:77 "| INV-7 | No blank publisher rows | Publishing ledger | Where a writer is unpublished, their publisher share is **auto-created as self-held** (D-03). Absent rows are the origin of black-box money. |"; D-03 at :298 "Unpublished writers' publisher shares are **auto-created as self-held**, never left blank"; edge case at :209 "| Publishing ledger with no publisher rows | **Valid** - unpublished writers self-hold their publisher share. Rows auto-created as self-held (D-03, INV-7). | Rows appear **pre-filled** with an explanation ('You hold your own publishing'), never left blank. |" || REQUIRES DECLARATION - 09.01-rights-registry/09.01.04-publishing-rights.md:196 "| Partial | Writers set, one or more publishing positions **undeclared** | Writer shares shown; 'Publishing position not declared' per row - **never** rendered as self-published. Ledger cannot leave `proposed` |"; edge case at :182 "| Work has a writer who is not on WeJammin | Invited stub; ledger stays `proposed`; **no publisher row can be anchored to them until they declare** ... Their publishing position is shown as **undeclared**, not as self-published - silence reads as silence. |"; Happy Path step 4 at :146 "Each writer is prompted - individually, on their own row - to declare their publishing position. **Self-published is one tap** (D-02); **it creates** a self-held publisher row anchored to them for their full publisher points."
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent whether the validator materialises publisher rows on behalf of silent writers. Under 09.01.02 the ledger validates and Propose unlocks with no writer having answered; under 09.01.04 the ledger is stuck in Partial until every writer taps. The two produce different ledgers, different `proposed` transitions, and - because 09.01.04 D-11 makes every anchored publisher a consent-holder on future amendments - different consent sets forever after. Domain D-06 ('silence must read as silence', rights-ownership-index.md:124) points at 09.01.04, but 09.01.02 is the file that owns the invariants.
findings.howToFix: Restate INV-7 and D-03 to fire only on a *declared* self-published position, and rewrite the :209 edge case so the pre-filled row is the one-tap default offered rather than a row the validator creates; or move the auto-creation into 09.01.04 as an explicit exception to domain D-06 with its reasoning stated.

Getting it wrong fires 09.01.02's non-dismissible 'Pair-incomplete' state (:251 'One of a work/recording ledger pair consented, the other `unallocated`' - 'Persistent... findings.claim: The live-set suggestion threshold is off by one against its own worked scenario: the scenario is a 12-song set for which the system 'suggests the better shape first', while the stated rule fires only above 12 linked works.
findings.evidence: 09.01-rights-registry/09.01.01-work-recording-duality.md:322 "| Live set recorded as one continuous file containing **12 songs** | Supported as a 12-work medley, but **the system suggests the better shape first**. | **Above 12 linked works**: 'This looks like a set, not a medley. Splitting it into one recording per song will pay everyone more accurately.' Suggestion only - never forced. |"
findings.forcedInvention: At exactly 12 linked works - the case the row is written about - an implementer must invent whether the split suggestion appears. One reads the scenario column and fires at >=12; the other reads the mechanism and fires at >12, in which case the row's own example silently produces no suggestion.
findings.howToFix: Pick one boundary and state it once - either change the mechanism to 'At 12 or more linked works' or change the scenario to 13 songs.

Defaulting to perpetual is the platform silently choosing the most extinguishing term available (DT-07, D-10). | 'Forever, or for a term?' - **required, unfilled**. |"; D-10 at :221 "**Perpetuity is an affirmed term**, never a default". || PRE-FILLS - 09.02-split-capture-agreements/09.02.03-work-for-hire-buyout.md:30 "The Operator configures their studio's standard WFH terms once (label, **perpetuity**, beneficiary = the studio entity); those terms then **pre-fill** whenever the studio's staff work a session."; edge case at :131 "Terms shown as **pre-filled** and editable, never silently applied."
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent whether a studio-configured perpetuity satisfies the 'required, unfilled' gate at :129 or whether the Producer must re-affirm it per designation. The staff engineer being bought out sees a pre-selected 'perpetual' in the first case and an empty required field in the second - which is precisely the difference D-10's rationale turns on.

findings.claim: The producer-points `base` - a required, never-defaulted term whose whole purpose is to name which waterfall tier a participation sits in - is enumerated with a third value ('the artist's share') that does not match the third tier the consuming waterfall defines ('owners' share').
findings.evidence: 09.02-split-capture-agreements/09.02.02-producer-points-agreements.md:47 "- **Base** - points *of what*? **Gross receipts, net receipts, or the artist's share.** These produce wildly different money from the same number, and the ambiguity is the dispute."; restated in the edge case at :67 "'Points of what? **Gross, net, or artist's share**' - required, unfilled." || The consuming tier model at 09.01-rights-registry/09.01.03-master-rights-ownership.md:188 is "gross receipts  ->  net receipts  ->  **owners' share**", with D-04 at :331 "Encumbrance burden is a **base-tiered waterfall** with a per-tier <=100% invariant" and the cross-cut at :307 "a **cleared** master sample creates a master-use obligation that enters this feature's waterfall **at the tier of its recorded base**".
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent the mapping. On a label-owned or investor-owned master the 'artist' and the 'owners' are different parties, so 'points of the artist's share' has no unambiguous tier - which reintroduces exactly the ambiguity 09.02.02 D-01 (:106) exists to eliminate ('Points of gross vs net vs artist's share are different money from an identical record').
findings.howToFix: Use one vocabulary for the tier in both files - most likely 'owners' share', since 09.01.03 owns the waterfall and its own worked example already reads '5 points of the owners' share to a featured artist'.

findings.claim: Two different consent-chase schedules are imposed on the one shared Consent Chase mechanism the domain routes out, with no note that they differ or why.
findings.evidence: DOMAIN-IMPOSED SCHEDULE - rights-ownership-cx.md:289 "| **Consent Chase & Escalating Notification** | 02, 05, 09, 11, 17 | ... **Requirements this domain imposes**: schedule **T+0/1d/3d/7d/14d/30d -> monthly to 12mo -> quarterly indefinitely**; **no expiry**...", restated verbatim at 09.02-split-capture-agreements/09.02.01-moment-of-creation-split-capture.md:112-118 and :235. || DIVERGENT SCHEDULE - 09.02-split-capture-agreements/09.02.04-split-amendment-reconsent.md:172 "| A party is **unreachable** ... | No consent -> no amendment. **Notices at day 0, day 7, day 21** on every channel on file. **At day 45** with zero interaction the proposal is badged `blocked`. |", carried into the States table at :221 "| Blocked | **45 days** with zero interaction from a required consenter..."
findings.forcedInvention: Day 21 and day 45 appear in neither the domain-imposed schedule nor 09.02.01's. An implementer building the single shared mechanism must invent whether amendment chases follow the domain schedule, whether the domain schedule is capture-specific, or whether two chase engines exist - and the `blocked` badge at day 45 has no counterpart in the capture flow at all, so it is unclear whether it is a chase property or an amendment-only state.
findings.howToFix: Either state in 09.02.04 that amendment consciously imposes a different cadence on the shared mechanism and why, or align it with the domain requirement in rights-ownership-cx.md:289 and keep the `blocked` badge as the only amendment-specific addition.
